thread:
maria.g: Customer on paid tier hit repeated streaming truncation + reconnect loops. They see SSE payload stop mid-event after ~28-35s, then client reconnects and gets 499/502 from origin intermittently. Reported from EU Cloudflare region -> ALB -> origin.

maria.g: Repro steps they gave:
```
# simple repro curl from a host in same region as CF
curl -sS -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  'https://api.redwood.example/chat/stream?session=abc' --no-buffer
```

maria.g: Observed headers/snippet from truncated stream:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Connection: keep-alive
X-Accel-Buffering: no

data: {"delta":"Hello, this is a par"
# stream stops here, client reconnects and receives 502 from ALB origin for first reconnect attempt
```

support-bot: Ticket #CS-3245 created and attached logs (customer provided).

chris.t: Interesting — they mention Cloudflare + ALB. Could be CF idle window vs ALB idle timeout vs NLB half-close race. Any upstream tcp FIN/half-close traces?

maria.g: Customer captured tcpdump on their client side and we saw FIN from ALB 1s before truncation. They said ALB idle timeout is default (60s) but stream cutting earlier ~30s. CF reports origin keepalive reuse and http/2 upgrade at the edge.

devon.k: A few sanity checks: 1) Is our runtime doing periodic no-op bytes (heartbeats) in the SSE? 2) Is CF buffering/HTTP/2 connection switching causing mid-chunk coalescing with proxies?

samir: We do send a `:\n` comment heartbeat every 15s on long SSEs. So shouldn't be idle. But if proxy buffers and then triggers a half-close on its TCP path, the chunk may be dropped after partial write.

devon.k: Can we get request/response path headers from a failing request? Specifically: `Via`, `Connection`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Content-Length`, and any CF/ALB intermediate headers. Also check if there is any gzip/deflate applied by an edge accelerator.

maria.g: Attached sample (redacted):
```
:cf-ray: 7a2bcd4e8
via: 1.1 cloudflare
x-amzn-trace-id: Root=1-abcdef
x-forwarded-for: 34.203.12.1
x-alb-tg: tg-xyz
server: awselb/2.0
content-encoding: gzip
```

chris.t: content-encoding: gzip on chunked SSE is a red flag. Many proxies will buffer to decompress/ recompress which breaks flush semantics. Cloudflare will buffer when compressing/transforming. If CF edge applied gzip, the origin may send small chunks that are coalesced into a single compressed frame — a partial flush could be lost on intermediate close.

devon.k: Two likely culprits then: (A) Edge applies compression and buffers, then a connection handoff (h2->h1) causes backpressure and a half-close, or (B) ALB/NLB/Envoy is configured with `proxy_buffering` or `sendfile` style optimizations. Check ALB idle/target group deregistration delay and backend keepalive settings.

maria.g: Customer confirmed they enabled "Auto Minify" and Brotli on CF. They turned them off for the route and reported immediate improvement in a quick test (no truncation in 3 attempts).

support-bot: Noted: toggling CF minify/Brotli mitigated in-customer test. Ticket updated.

samir: OK promising. We should still reproduce in a controlled lab: create CF Worker that toggles brotli/minify and ALB in front of a simple SSE app that sends a long 1-token-per-250ms stream. Use `wrk` or a curl loop to detect mid-event truncation.

devon.k: Also add a test with `Connection: keep-alive`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, and explicit `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Try with/without `Content-Encoding`. If compression is on, proxies will buffer a full gzip frame before forwarding. That explains the mid-chunk drop — because the compressed frame is incomplete when upstream drops.

chris.t: Operational fix recommendations to customer for now: 1) disable CF compression/minify for SSE endpoints; 2) set ALB target group `keep-alive` higher (>= 120s); 3) enable `proxy_buffering off` for nginx/Envoy if used between CF and origin.

maria.g: I'll propose a changelist to the customer with those three items. They've asked for an internal RCA and reproducible steps so they can document for their ops team.

devon.k: For our side, file an infra playbook note: SSE endpoints must avoid edge compression and use heartbeat comments. Add an alert if we detect >1% sessions truncated mid-event with immediate reconnects.

chris.t: Also worth adding a note to docs: "If using Cloudflare or similar edge, disable content transformations (Brotli/gzip/minify) for streaming endpoints." Might prevent a bunch of tickets.

maria.g: I'll push a draft doc and the reproducible test harness to the internal repo. Closing this thread once customer validates change. :thumbsup:

ingress-bot: Deployed test harness env `sse-repro-v2` to staging (svc-port 8080) at 2026-03-10T02:12:00Z.

maria.g: Thanks — leaving note for follow-up validation tomorrow.
